title: MProt-DPO: Breaking the ExaFLOPS Barrier for Multimodal Protein Design Workflows with Direct Preference Optimization
problem: Protein design workflows lack scalability to ExaFLOPS performance levels. Integrating experimental and simulation-based fitness constraints into generative protein design requires efficient multimodal alignment of sequences with biochemical property descriptions.
motivation: Accelerating protein design through ExaFLOPS-scale computation enables faster iteration in drug discovery, enzyme engineering, and synthetic biology.
method: The workflow augments protein sequences with natural language descriptions of biochemical properties and trains generative models using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to align with protein fitness landscapes. Experimental and simulation-based observations are integrated as preferred parameters for generating new protein variants. Mixed-precision computing is optimized across distributed supercomputer architectures to achieve sustained ExaFLOPS performance.
key_novelty: First application of Direct Preference Optimization to multimodal protein design achieving ExaFLOPS-scale sustained performance across multiple diverse supercomputers.
contributions: Scalable end-to-end protein design workflow achieving >1 ExaFLOPS sustained performance in mixed precision across five supercomputers
Multimodal approach combining protein sequences with natural language descriptions for improved generative model fitness alignment
Demonstration on HIS7 deep mutational scanning optimization and malate dehydrogenase catalytic rate improvement using simulation data
Peak performance of 5.57 ExaFLOPS and sustained performance of 4.11 ExaFLOPS

metrics.other: 4.11 ExaFLOPS sustained, 5.57 ExaFLOPS peak, >1 ExaFLOPS sustained minimum across all systems

primary_theme: Multimodal protein design at ExaFLOPS scale using preference optimization
